Starts with H. A four-letter cry heard by every new hire staring at an inbox of 400. Try the obvious.

puzzles.description: Talk to Sam. They introduce Amazon Quick and explain what to do next.

config.name: Sam
config.greeting: Oh hey. You found the desk. Yeah — that mailbox looks like a war crime. Don't panic. There's a trick, and it's called Amazon Quick. Also, no — not QuickSight. QuickSight does dashboards. Quick is the whole work companion. It's here to save your morning.

lines.label: What is Amazon Quick, exactly?
lines.response: AI work companion. It sits on top of our data — churn reports, network tickets, exec asks, the whole internal doc system — and you ask it questions in plain English. It goes and reads everything relevant and comes back with an answer. Not a search bar. More like a colleague who already read every doc last night.

lines.label: So it's the same as QuickSight?
lines.response: It USES QuickSight for charts, yes. But Quick itself is the whole suite. Three things it does: Research — go find and summarize stuff. Dashboards — read them AND build them. Automate — schedule things, draft things on repeat. Any ask you have, it falls into one of those three buckets. Know the bucket, know how to ask.

lines.label: How do I ask it something good?
lines.response: Four parts, in this order. Action — a verb Quick can do, like 'summarize' or 'find'. Subject — the actual thing, like 'last month's churn'. Context — which slice, 'for the northern region', 'this quarter', 'for enterprise'. Format — how you want it back, '3 bullets', 'a chart', 'a paragraph'. Skip a part, mid answer. Include all four, scary-good answer.

lines.label: Does it actually know OUR stuff?
lines.response: Yeah, that was the whole rollout last quarter — we plugged Quick into the internal doc system. It reads current churn data, latest network reports, this quarter's KPIs. It also reads five-year-old pricing sheets and duplicate exports if we don't clean them up, so — you'll see. Right context in, brilliant Quick. Fire hose of everything, confused Quick.

lines.label: Where do I start?
lines.response: Two things right here on my desk. Sort what Quick can do into the three buckets — you'll see six real analyst asks and where each one belongs. Then draft your first ask to Quick using the four-parts rule. Do both and you're ready to actually hit the inbox. Go. I'll grab coffee. You've got this.

hints: Click each option to hear Sam. The three-bucket answer and the four-part prompt structure both show up early.
Sam names the three buckets: Research, Dashboards, Automate. And names the four prompt parts: Action, Subject, Context, Format.
Read every dialog line — the answers to both puzzles in this room are literally in Sam's dialog.

puzzles.description: Six real analyst asks. Sort each into the correct Quick capability bucket: Research, Dashboards, or Automate.

pillar_wrong_feedback.Research: Research = summarize / find / explain why. Try again.
pillar_wrong_feedback.Dashboards: Dashboards = show / chart / live view of a metric. Try again.
pillar_wrong_feedback.Automate: Automate = recurring / auto-draft / do it every time. Try again.

statements.text: Summarize why churn spiked in the northern region last month

wrong_feedback.Dashboards: 'Summarize why' is a Research verb — you want an explanation, not a chart.
wrong_feedback.Automate: It's a one-shot ask, not a schedule — that puts it in Research.

statements.text: Show me this quarter's ARPU trend as a chart

wrong_feedback.Research: 'Show me' + 'as a chart' is Dashboards — pictures of a metric, not a summary.
wrong_feedback.Automate: There's no schedule and no draft — it's a one-off view. That's Dashboards.

statements.text: Every Monday, email me the top 10 escalated tickets

wrong_feedback.Research: 'Every Monday' is the tell — that's a recurring schedule, i.e. Automate.
wrong_feedback.Dashboards: It's a recurring email, not a live chart on a screen. That's Automate.

statements.text: Find the 3 root causes buyers cite for cancelling

wrong_feedback.Dashboards: 'Find … root causes' asks for an explanation — that's Research, not a chart.
wrong_feedback.Automate: One-time investigation, not something you run on a schedule — Research.

statements.text: Build a live view of network outage tickets by state

wrong_feedback.Research: 'Live view … by state' is a dashboard — an updating picture of a metric.
wrong_feedback.Automate: It's a persistent view, not a recurring draft or scheduled action — Dashboards.

statements.text: Auto-draft replies to billing complaints for my review

wrong_feedback.Research: 'Auto-draft … for my review' is a recurring draft — that's Automate.
wrong_feedback.Dashboards: Drafts and replies aren't charts — that's Automate.

hints: Three buckets. Research = go look things up and summarize. Dashboards = show me numbers as pictures. Automate = do this on a schedule, or draft this for me every time.
Verb clues: 'summarize' / 'find' / 'why' → Research. 'Show me' / 'chart' / 'live view' → Dashboards. 'Every Monday' / 'auto-draft' / 'schedule' → Automate.
Research: churn summary, root causes. Dashboards: ARPU chart, live outage view. Automate: Monday email, auto-drafted billing replies.

puzzles.description: Assemble your first good ask to Quick — one choice per slot. Great asks have four parts.

config.success_response: 🥇 Perfect ask. Action + subject + context + format — all four slots specific. Quick returns three tight bullets on last month's northern churn in eight seconds. That's the whole trick.
config.partial_response: 🥈 Close. Quick returns something — but not sharp. A specific action, a real subject, a real scope, and the format you actually want gets you a scary-good answer. Tighten the weak slots.
config.fail_response: ❌ Quick can't find your intent. A great ask has four parts — an action, a subject, a scope/context, and a format. 'Vibe check', 'kinda', 'everywhere all at once', 'no format' — those aren't asks, those are shrugs. Try again.

hints: Great asks have four parts: Action, Subject, Context, Format. Quick works best when all four are specific.

Action = a verb Quick can actually do ('summarize', not 'vibe check'). Subject = a real thing (churn, not 'my feelings'). Context = a real slice (northern region, not 'everywhere all at once'). Format = how you want it back (3 bullets, not 'no format').
Row by row: Summarize / last month's churn / for the northern region / in 3 bullet points.
